fact: Lebanon's National Water Strategy 2024-2035 identifies four pillars: enhanced water security, improved provision of public services, sustainable utilities, and good governance/leadership.
operational_implication: Use as sector policy context only; do not route citizen field complaints to MEW just because a case concerns national strategy.
notes: MEW is policy lead; WEs remain first-line operational entities for ordinary complaints.

fact: The 2024-2035 strategy targets reducing non-revenue water by 25 percentage points from an estimated national average of 50% by 2035.
operational_implication: Leaks and illegal connections are sector-priority issues, but no individual repair SLA is implied.
notes: Useful for prioritization and analytics; not promise-making.

fact: The 2024-2035 strategy targets full digital transformation of Water Establishments by 2035.
operational_implication: Digital channels may expand over time; keep app/e-service facts date-stamped and source-backed.
notes: Supports periodic refresh of online channel inventory.

fact: The 2024-2035 strategy targets reducing water-sector energy cost by 30% through efficiency and renewable-energy practices by 2035.
operational_implication: Power-related pumping failures are plausible operational context, but citizen routing remains to the relevant WE unless clear EDL/public-safety evidence exists.
notes: Do not convert water outages into electricity complaints automatically.

fact: The 2024-2035 strategy places water quality high in MEW priorities and refers to a national water quality monitoring plan.
operational_implication: Dirty-water complaints should remain WE-primary with HITL/public-health/MOE escalation when contamination scope is broader than a tap/building.
notes: Strategy source is policy-level; not a local incident-intake page.

fact: The 2025 World Bank Second Greater Beirut Water Supply Project aims to improve services for 1.8 million people in Greater Beirut and Mount Lebanon and raise dry-season surface water supply share from 24% to 70% on average.
operational_implication: Use for BMLWE strategic service context; do not promise improved service to a specific citizen complaint.
notes: World Bank institutional source; project benefits are program targets.

fact: The World Bank states the project supports BMLWE efficiency measures: reducing water losses, digitalizing processes, enhancing billing and collection, and improving operational management.
operational_implication: Use to justify tracking BMLWE loss, billing, and digital-service evidence over time.
notes: Not a complaint SLA.

fact: The World Bank Lake Qaraoun project objective is to reduce untreated municipal sewage discharged into the Litani River and improve pollution management around Qaraoun Lake.
operational_implication: River/Litani/Qaraoun pollution complaints need LRA/MOE/HITL boundary handling rather than ordinary household WE routing alone.
notes: Supports environmental boundary conditions.

fact: UNICEF states Lebanon's public water systems have struggled to consistently operate pumps, treat water effectively, or conduct maintenance since the crisis started in 2019.
operational_implication: Keep restoration-time claims conservative; outages may reflect energy, fuel, repair, or treatment constraints.
notes: Institutional context; not entity-specific SLA.

fact: UNICEF states many households depend on costly and often poor-quality private water trucking because public systems are strained.
operational_implication: Private water-truck complaints should not be routed to WEs unless the complaint concerns public-network failure or official service substitution.
notes: Useful false-positive guardrail.

fact: UNICEF reports 2024 WASH support including over 500 water-system repairs, solarization of 14 water stations, support to 16 wastewater treatment plants, chlorine supplies, lab equipment, and coordination with WEs.
operational_implication: Trusted evidence that WEs rely on partner support during crisis; do not infer official citizen response times.
notes: Keep as sector-resilience context.

fact: UNICEF states chlorine support was coordinated with NLWE as part of cholera prevention and response.
operational_implication: Water-quality or disease-risk complaints in NLWE area should carry public-health/HITL sensitivity when symptoms or outbreak language appears.
notes: Operational inference from institutional programme text.

fact: UNICEF states it offered technical support and ad-hoc coordination in collaboration with BMLWE.
operational_implication: Use as partner-support context, not as a direct complaint channel.
notes: No citizen-facing UNICEF routing.

fact: UNICEF's 2024 emergency release says water facilities were damaged and water supply was affected for more than 360,000 people, primarily in the south, during the escalation.
operational_implication: In conflict/damage contexts, water outage routing should allow emergency/HITL handling and avoid routine SLA assumptions.
notes: Context may become stale; refresh if using for real-time response.

fact: UNICEF states supplies were handed to MEW to strengthen Water Establishments' capacity for rapid emergency repairs during the emergency.
operational_implication: Use as evidence that MEW can coordinate emergency support while WEs remain operational implementers.
notes: Not a public intake process.

fact: UNICEF emergency response reporting cites support to Water Establishments with repairs, fuel, pumps, chlorine, generators, and pipes during hostilities.
operational_implication: Emergency water complaints may involve damaged facilities and supply-chain constraints; route to WE plus HITL where safety or displacement context exists.
notes: Refresh before using as current situation.

fact: UNICEF's 2021 story says the four Water Establishments, with UNICEF/EU support, repaired leaking pipes and connected some homes to mains water.
operational_implication: Confirms WEs are the correct public-network repair actors; private internal plumbing remains out of scope.
notes: Background example; not current hotline data.

fact: UNICEF's 2021 story describes BWE coordination for rapid response to calls for improvements in the Zahle area and examples of new water-pipe connections.
operational_implication: Use as BWE operational-background evidence for public network leaks/connections, not as current SLA.
notes: Story-level institutional evidence.

fact: UNICEF's 2025 release says AFD, UNICEF, EU, and MEW support enabled Water Establishments to continue pumping and distributing water to over 1.5 million people.
operational_implication: Use for resilience and power-dependency context; do not infer household-level availability.
notes: Institutional support evidence.

fact: UNICEF reports solarization of 14 water stations, rehabilitation of eight water stations and one water channel, expansion of six gravity-fed networks, and installation of three new water systems.
operational_implication: Solar/power context can explain why electricity and water complaints overlap, but WE routing remains location/entity based.
notes: Programme-level scope; not an operations dispatch list.

fact: AFD's 2025 evaluation summary says its technical assistance programme supports priority water and sanitation reforms, capacity-building for RWEs, project maturation, and institutional dialogue with MEW.
operational_implication: Use as trusted reform context for why source refresh and governance fields matter.
notes: Evaluation summary is sector-level rather than citizen-facing.

fact: AFD describes its programme as targeting legislative framework, institutional capacity, and operational efficiency for MEW and the RWEs.
operational_implication: Use for long-term institutional context; do not alter routing by itself.
notes: No direct complaint channel.

fact: Oxfam says its support since 2015 focused chiefly on BWE but also targeted SLWE, NLWE, and BMLWE through infrastructure rehabilitation, technical staff secondment, and capacity development.
operational_implication: Use as external-support context when explaining why BWE and other WEs may have solarization/capacity-support footprints.
notes: Oxfam is trusted institutional evidence but not official authority.

fact: Oxfam identifies BWE as the chief focus of its Water Establishments support over the past decade.
operational_implication: Use for BWE resilience context; do not route BWE complaints to Oxfam.
notes: Evaluation context only.

fact: The World Bank RDNA covers the 2023-2024 conflict impacts across ten sectors, including water, wastewater, and irrigation, for damage losses and recovery needs.
operational_implication: Use for emergency/conflict context and reconstruction sensitivity in affected areas.
notes: Not a live damage map.

fact: The UNHCR Operational Data Portal hosts the Lebanon Response Plan WaSH Sector Dashboard for end-year 2025 covering Lebanon, North Lebanon, Beirut, South Lebanon, Bekaa, and Mount Lebanon.
operational_implication: Use as a trusted pointer for future humanitarian WASH metrics refresh.
notes: Dashboard is sector monitoring; not per-entity complaint policy.
